title.en: Have you ever seen a raven?
title.de: Das Present Perfect: have you ever, I've just
title.sl: Sedanji perfekt: have you ever, I've just
title.it: Il present perfect: have you ever, I've just

goal.sl: Govoriš o življenju doslej (I've seen a raven, Have you ever been to Keswick?, I've never been), poveš, kaj se je pravkar zgodilo in kaj še ne, in rabiš past simple, takoj ko poveš, kdaj.
goal.de: Du sprichst über dein Leben bis jetzt (I've seen a raven, Have you ever been to Keswick?, I've never been), sagst, was gerade passiert ist und was noch nicht, und nimmst das past simple, sobald du sagst, wann.
goal.it: Parli della tua vita finora (I've seen a raven, Have you ever been to Keswick?, I've never been), dici che cosa è appena successo e che cosa non ancora, e usi il past simple appena dici quando.
goal.en: You can talk about your life so far (I've seen a raven, Have you ever been to Keswick?, I've never been), say what has just happened and what hasn't yet, and use the past simple as soon as you say when.

say.sl: Za življenje doslej, brez časa: **have** ali **has** + deležnik (past participle). **I've seen a raven.** (Videl{m:|f:a} sem krokarja.) **She's climbed Helvellyn.** (Povzpela se je na Helvellyn.) **We've walked round the tarn.** (Obhodili smo jezerce.) Tu je **'s** has. Vedno have, nikoli be: **I've been**, nikoli *I am been*. Zanikano: **haven't**, **hasn't**. Deležnik pravilnega glagola je kot preteklik: **climbed**, **walked**.
say.de: Für dein Leben bis jetzt, ohne Zeitangabe: **have** oder **has** + Partizip (past participle). **I've seen a raven.** (Ich habe einen Raben gesehen.) **She's climbed Helvellyn.** (Sie ist auf den Helvellyn gestiegen.) **We've walked round the tarn.** (Wir sind um den Bergsee gegangen.) Hier ist **'s** has. Immer have, nie be: **I've been**, nie *I am been*. Verneint: **haven't**, **hasn't**. Bei regelmäßigen Verben ist das Partizip wie die Vergangenheit: **climbed**, **walked**.
say.it: Per la tua vita finora, senza dire quando: **have** o **has** + il participio (past participle). **I've seen a raven.** (Ho visto un corvo imperiale.) **She's climbed Helvellyn.** (È salita sull'Helvellyn.) **We've walked round the tarn.** (Abbiamo fatto il giro del laghetto.) Qui **'s** è has. Sempre have, mai be: **I've been**, mai *I am been*. Negativo: **haven't**, **hasn't**. Nei verbi regolari il participio è come il passato: **climbed**, **walked**.
say.en: For your life so far, with no time said: **have** or **has** + the past participle. **I've seen a raven.** **She's climbed Helvellyn.** **We've walked round the tarn.** Always have, never be: **I've been** (never *I am been*). Here **'s** is has. No: **haven't**, **hasn't**. A regular verb's participle looks like its past: **climbed**, **walked**.

say.sl: Mnogi deležniki so kot preteklik: **made**, **met**, **had**, **heard**, **found**. Drugi imajo svojo obliko, ki se je naučiš: see → **seen**, be → **been**, do → **done**, eat → **eaten**, take → **taken**, write → **written**. Nikoli preteklik: **I've seen**, nikoli *I've saw*. Pri go sta dve obliki: **He's gone to Keswick.** (Šel je v Keswick in je še tam.) **He's been to Keswick.** (Bil je v Keswicku in se je vrnil.)
say.de: Viele Partizipien sehen aus wie die Vergangenheit: **made**, **met**, **had**, **heard**, **found**. Andere haben eine eigene Form, die du einzeln lernst: see → **seen**, be → **been**, do → **done**, eat → **eaten**, take → **taken**, write → **written**. Nie die Vergangenheit: **I've seen**, nie *I've saw*. Bei go gibt es zwei: **He's gone to Keswick.** (Er ist nach Keswick gefahren und noch dort.) **He's been to Keswick.** (Er war in Keswick und ist wieder da.)
say.it: Molti participi sono come il passato: **made**, **met**, **had**, **heard**, **found**. Altri hanno una forma loro, da imparare una per una: see → **seen**, be → **been**, do → **done**, eat → **eaten**, take → **taken**, write → **written**. Mai il passato: **I've seen**, mai *I've saw*. Con go ce ne sono due: **He's gone to Keswick.** (È andato a Keswick ed è ancora lì.) **He's been to Keswick.** (È stato a Keswick ed è tornato.)
say.en: Many participles look like the past: **made**, **met**, **had**, **heard**, **found**. Others have their own form, learned one by one: see → **seen**, be → **been**, do → **done**, eat → **eaten**, take → **taken**, write → **written**. Never the past instead: **I've seen** (never *I've saw*). And go has two: **He's gone to Keswick.** (he's still there) **He's been to Keswick.** (and he's back)

say.sl: Ko sprašuješ za vse življenje: **Have you ever seen a raven?** (Si že kdaj videl{m:|f:a} krokarja?) **Has Jack ever been to London?** (Je bil Jack že kdaj v Londonu?) Odgovor: **Yes, I have.** (Ja.) **No, I haven't.** (Ne.) **never** je že sam ne, slovenski *nikoli nisem* pa ima dva: **I've never been to Carlisle.** (Nikoli nisem bil{m:|f:a} v Carlislu.) Nikoli *I haven't never been*. **ever** in **never** stojita pred deležnikom.
say.de: Wenn du nach dem ganzen Leben fragst: **Have you ever seen a raven?** (Hast du schon einmal einen Raben gesehen?) **Has Jack ever been to London?** (War Jack schon einmal in London?) Die Antwort: **Yes, I have.** (Ja.) **No, I haven't.** (Nein.) **never** ist schon das Nein, ohne zweites not: **I've never been to Carlisle.** (Ich war noch nie in Carlisle.) Nie *I haven't never been*. **ever** und **never** stehen vor dem Partizip.
say.it: Per chiedere di tutta una vita: **Have you ever seen a raven?** (Hai mai visto un corvo imperiale?) **Has Jack ever been to London?** (Jack è mai stato a Londra?) La risposta: **Yes, I have.** (Sì.) **No, I haven't.** (No.) **never** è già il no, senza un altro not, dove l'italiano dice *non … mai*: **I've never been to Carlisle.** (Non sono mai stat{m:o|f:a} a Carlisle.) Mai *I haven't never been*. **ever** e **never** stanno prima del participio.
say.en: To ask about a whole life: **Have you ever seen a raven?** **Has Jack ever been to London?** The answer: **Yes, I have.** **No, I haven't.** **never** is the no, with no other not: **I've never been to Carlisle** (never *I haven't never been*). **ever** and **never** stand before the participle.

say.sl: **just** pomeni pravkar in stoji pred deležnikom: **I've just seen Jack.** (Pravkar sem videl{m:|f:a} Jacka.) **The bus has just left.** (Avtobus je pravkar odpeljal.) **Mrs Birkett has just made some tea.** (Gospa Birkett je pravkar skuhala čaj.) Američani rečejo tudi **I just saw Jack**, in tudi to je prav.
say.de: **just** heißt gerade eben und steht vor dem Partizip: **I've just seen Jack.** (Ich habe gerade Jack gesehen.) **The bus has just left.** (Der Bus ist gerade abgefahren.) **Mrs Birkett has just made some tea.** (Mrs Birkett hat gerade Tee gemacht.) Amerikanisch sagt man auch **I just saw Jack**, und auch das ist richtig.
say.it: **just** vuol dire appena e sta prima del participio: **I've just seen Jack.** (Ho appena visto Jack.) **The bus has just left.** (L'autobus è appena partito.) **Mrs Birkett has just made some tea.** (Mrs Birkett ha appena fatto il tè.) In americano si dice anche **I just saw Jack**, e va bene anche così.
say.en: **just** means a moment ago, and stands before the participle: **I've just seen Jack.** **The bus has just left.** **Mrs Birkett has just made some tea.** American English also says **I just saw Jack**, and that's right too.

say.sl: **already** (že) stoji pred deležnikom: **I've already eaten.** (Sem že {m:jedel|f:jedla}.) **yet** stoji na koncu, v vprašanju (že) in z not (še): **Have you fed the dogs yet, Jack?** (Si že nahranil pse, Jack?) **I haven't finished yet.** (Še nisem {m:končal|f:končala}.) Američani rečejo tudi **Did you feed the dogs yet?**
say.de: **already** (schon) steht vor dem Partizip: **I've already eaten.** (Ich habe schon gegessen.) **yet** steht am Ende, in der Frage (schon) und mit not (noch nicht): **Have you fed the dogs yet, Jack?** (Hast du die Hunde schon gefüttert, Jack?) **I haven't finished yet.** (Ich bin noch nicht fertig.) Amerikanisch auch **Did you feed the dogs yet?**
say.it: **already** (già) sta prima del participio: **I've already eaten.** (Ho già mangiato.) **yet** va alla fine, nella domanda (già) e con not (non ancora): **Have you fed the dogs yet, Jack?** (Hai già dato da mangiare ai cani, Jack?) **I haven't finished yet.** (Non ho ancora finito.) In americano anche **Did you feed the dogs yet?**
say.en: **already** stands before the participle: **I've already eaten.** **yet** goes at the end, in a question and with not: **Have you fed the dogs yet, Jack?** **I haven't finished yet** (never *I've finished yet*). American English also says **Did you feed the dogs yet?**

say.sl: Takoj ko poveš, kdaj, pride **past simple** (slovenščina ima za oboje en čas): **I saw a raven yesterday.** (Včeraj sem videl{m:|f:a} krokarja.) Nikoli *I've seen a raven yesterday*. Besede za kdaj: **yesterday**, **last week**, **two days ago**, **in 2019**. Pogovor se pogosto začne s perfektom in gre naprej v pretekliku: **Have you ever been to Keswick? — Yes, I went there last week.** (Ja, tja sem {m:šel|f:šla} prejšnji teden.)
say.de: Sobald du sagst, wann, kommt das **past simple**, auch wo Deutsch das Perfekt nimmt: **I saw a raven yesterday.** (Ich habe gestern einen Raben gesehen.) Nie *I've seen a raven yesterday*. Wörter für wann: **yesterday**, **last week**, **two days ago**, **in 2019**. Ein Gespräch beginnt oft im present perfect und geht in der Vergangenheit weiter: **Have you ever been to Keswick? — Yes, I went there last week.** (Ja, ich war letzte Woche dort.)
say.it: Appena dici quando, viene il **past simple**, anche dove l'italiano dice sempre *ho visto*: **I saw a raven yesterday.** (Ieri ho visto un corvo imperiale.) Mai *I've seen a raven yesterday*. Le parole del quando: **yesterday**, **last week**, **two days ago**, **in 2019**. Una conversazione comincia spesso col present perfect e continua al passato: **Have you ever been to Keswick? — Yes, I went there last week.** (Sì, ci sono stat{m:o|f:a} la settimana scorsa.)
say.en: As soon as you say when, the past simple comes: **I saw a raven yesterday** (never *I've seen a raven yesterday*). The when-words: **yesterday**, **last week**, **two days ago**, **in 2019**. So talk often begins with the present perfect and goes on in the past: **Have you ever been to Keswick? — Yes, I went there last week.** British English keeps the two apart.

translation.sl: — Ste že kdaj bili v Lake Districtu? — Ne, nisem. Prvič sem tukaj. — Ste se že povzpeli na Helvellyn? — Še ne! Sem pa že {m:obhodil|f:obhodila} jezerce in pravkar {m:videl|f:videla} krokarja. — Krokarja! Jaz sem enega videla prejšnji teden na hribu. Skuhala sem juho. Bi je malo?
translation.de: — Waren Sie schon einmal im Lake District? — Nein. Ich bin zum ersten Mal hier. — Waren Sie schon auf dem Helvellyn? — Noch nicht! Aber ich bin schon um den Bergsee gegangen und habe gerade einen Raben gesehen. — Einen Raben! Ich habe letzte Woche einen am Berg gesehen. Ich habe Suppe gemacht. Möchten Sie welche?
translation.it: — È mai stat{m:o|f:a} nel Lake District? — No. È la prima volta. — È già salit{m:o|f:a} sull'Helvellyn? — Non ancora! Ma ho già fatto il giro del laghetto e ho appena visto un corvo imperiale. — Un corvo imperiale! Io ne ho visto uno la settimana scorsa, sul monte. Ho fatto la zuppa. Ne vuole un po'?
translation.en: — Have you ever been to the Lakes? — No, I haven't. This is my first time. — Have you climbed Helvellyn? — Not yet! But I've already walked round the tarn, and I've just seen a raven. — A raven! I saw one last week, on the fell. I've made some soup. Would you like some?
